reason: The first reading saw only line-ends and could not connect them; with the printed gloss open, provinciales became principales, the repeated ac. was recognised as Accursius's signature, and the cross-references fell into place.
sources: Volumen legum parvum ... cum commentariis Accursii (1566), Authenticorum Collatio nona, tit. 4-5 (Nov. 125, 124), col. 471-472, BSB bsb11057347, image 420
Volumen legum parvum (1566), Collatio nona, tit. 3 (Nov. 120 c. 9-11), col. 469-470, BSB bsb11057347, image 419 (main-text lead only)

F-cjzj. Source-assisted reading. All 25 line-ends of the strip were reread on the image by a research reader; lines 1-5 before the source was found, lines 6-25 with the 1566 Volumen (BSB bsb11057347, image 420, col. 471) open. The other face (canvas 1) was not reread to a usable standard and is not included. Accuracy has not been measured.
( ) expansion; [ ] hidden under the pastedown, lost or supplied; ? uncertain. | marks the edge of the pastedown; everything to its left is hidden.
